item.title: Giants sign S Tavierre Thomas off Vikings practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Giants are adding some depth for their secondary.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants are adding some depth for their secondary.

New York is signing safety Tavierre Thomas off of Minnesota's practice squad, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

Thomas has appeared in one game for the Vikings this season, playing 24 special teams snaps.

Thomas, 30, has appeared in 116 career games with 22 starts for the Browns, Texans, Bucs, and Vikings. He’s tallied six passes defensed, seven forced fumbles, and two interceptions.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Seattle may not have one of its offensive and special teams contributors when the club returns from its Week 11 bye.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle may not have one of its offensive and special teams contributors when the club returns from its Week 11 bye.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, running back George Holani suffered an MCL sprain during Sunday’s win over the Raiders.

He is considered week-to-week with the injury.

Because the Seahawks are on their bye, the club is hoping Holani will not need to be placed on injured reserve. But the club will evaluate the situation next week.

Holani has appeared in 10 games this season, recording 117 yards on 37 carries with a touchdown. He’s also caught 12 passes for 88 yards.

item.title: Sean Payton: "There's no loophole" in the trade process
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Payton disputes JIm Harbaugh's characterization of the failed Daiyan Henley trade.
item.content:encoded:
After last week's failed trade that would have sent Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos, L.A. coach Jim Harbaugh said that the Broncos used a "loophole" to squeeze the Chargers into better terms before the deal imploded.

The Broncos had no comment last week, and coach Sean Payton hadn't spoken to reporters because Denver had a Week 10 bye.

On Monday, Payton was available to the media. And the first question asked what changed as to the Henley trade.

“Nothing changed," Payton said. "It was already stated. Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought — and still do [think] — very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.”

So is there a loophole?

“There’s no loophole," Payton said. "It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.”

He's technically right, but there is a loophole. A team that has buyer's remorse can try to rely on issues with the physical to negotiate better terms. And an unscrupulous team could finalize a deal before the deadline with the plan of trying to improve the deal later, under the guise of a failed physical.

The easy fix, when it comes to deadline deals, is to take the position that, after the window for making trades closes, the player either passes the physical and the trade goes through as negotiated or the player fails the physical and the deal dies.

There should be no "maybe" box when it comes to physicals. Especially after the period for making trades has ended.

item.title: Jordan Addison to miss multiple weeks after thumb surgery
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison's thumb injury kept him from playing in Sunday's win over the Packers and it will be a little while before he's able to return to action.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison's thumb injury kept him from playing in Sunday's win over the Packers and it will be a little while before he's able to return to action.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell said at a Monday press conference that Addison needs to have surgery after hurting his thumb in practice on Friday. O'Connell said Addison will miss multiple weeks as a result.

If Addison goes on injured reserve, he will have to miss at least four more games due to the injury. The Vikings play the 49ers, Falcons, Panthers and Patriots over the next four weeks.

Addison has 18 catches for 277 yards and a touchdown this season. Justin Jefferson, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones were the Vikings' receivers on Sunday with Addison and Jauan Jennings out of action.

item.title: Mike Macdonald "really optimistic" Sam Darnold will be able to return Week 12
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Seahawks are anticipating having Sam Darnold back for their next game.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks are anticipating having Sam Darnold back for their next game.

Seattle will have its bye in Week 11. But head coach Mike Macdonald said in an interview with Seattle Sports 710 on Monday that Darnold could be back for the Week 12 matchup against the 49ers.

"I’d say we’re really optimistic that he’s going to be able to get a full week’s worth of work and be able to play against San Francisco,” Macdonald said, via John Boyle of the team’s website.

Macdonald also noted that backup Drew Lock won’t be replacing Darnold, saying, “Sam’s our starting quarterback.”

Darnold has missed the last two games with quad and rib injuries.

While Darnold’s performance has dipped in 2026, Macdonald has been steadfast in his support of the quarterback the club won the Super Bowl with in February.

Seattle is 3-4 in Darnold’s starts this season — with Drew Lock playing most of the Week 1 win over New England. Darnold has completed 60.2 percent of his passes for 1,478 yards with 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions this season.

Lock, however, sports a 3-0 record this season. He’s completed 73.1 percent of his throws for 837 yards with seven touchdowns and no picks.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Eagles announced a handful of roster moves as they come out of their bye week.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles announced a handful of roster moves as they come out of their bye week.

They have signed tight end Zach Ertz and offensive tackle John Ojukwu to the active roster. They have also designated running back Will Shipley for return from injured reserve.

Ertz returned to the organization via the practice squad in September and was elevated to play in three games. He had three catches for 22 yards in those appearances.

Ojukwu has been on the practice squad since failing to make the team out of the summer, but has not appeared in any games. He played in 16 games for the Titans over the past three seasons.

Shipley had 20 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the first five games. He has missed the last four games with a foot injury.

item.title: UFL's BattleHawks work out a deal to stay at dome in St. Louis
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As of last month, the UFL had a stadium issue in St.
item.content:encoded:
As of last month, the UFL had a stadium issue in St. Louis. As of now, it's resolved.

Via Fox 2 in St. Louis, the UFL and the powers-that-be have struck a deal to create better flexibility in the scheduling of five BattleHawks home games at The Dome at America’s Center.

Under the prior schedule, the BattleHawks would have played four straight home games, followed by five straight road games, capped by a home game. The details of the revised schedule have not yet been announced.

UFL co-owner Mike Repole, who has been aggressively using Twitter to market the league and to squabble directly with critics, took a social-media victory lap.

“We weren’t going to settle," he posted. "We pushed for better. We got it done!!!! A BIG THANK YOU to our partners at The Dome at America’s Center.”

While the UFL is largely a made-for-TV league, it has been trying to create better visuals by playing in stadiums that are easier to fill. The size of the dome in St. Louis makes that harder. Stacking four home games together in four straight weekends won't make that any easier.

item.title: Packers, Rams embark on shortest possible bye weeks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In Week 11, six teams will have a bye.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 11, six teams will have a bye. Four will have a full, two-week break. Two will have the shortest possible bye weeks.

It's the latest byproduct of the effort to find more places in the pizza into which cheese can be crammed (and/or from which cash can be siphoned).

The NFL will play its first-ever game on the night before Thanksgiving. The easiest, and more equitable, approach to scheduling entailed giving the Week 12 Wednesday assignment to teams that don't play in Week 11.

Still, it's not a real bye week. The Rams and Packers will play 10 days after their pre-bye games. The usual in-season break is 14 days.

It's possible that a team could play on Monday night and the next Thursday, 10 days later. We're not aware of that happening since the NFL embraced full-season Thursday night games; usually, the league tries to have the same amount of down time for both teams playing on a Thursday night.

Actually, the Packers will get more time off on the back end than the front end of their off week. Green Bay's Week 13 game comes 11 days after the Week 12 game.

The Rams won't be so lucky. They play the Chiefs on the following Thursday night, resulting in 10 days, 8 days, and 10 days between L.A. games.

But that's how it will go in the new and improved NFL. More windows. More prime-time games. More international games.

All with the objective of the ultimate more.

More money.

item.title: Mike Vrabel on Drake Maye: I wouldn't imagine him being available out of the bye
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There has been mixed reporting about the status of Drake Maye's ankle injury after the Patriots lost to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
There has been mixed reporting about the status of Drake Maye's ankle injury after the Patriots lost to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.

New England will be on its bye in Week 11. In his Monday press conference, head coach Mike Vrabel would only go as far as noting the quarterback's likely status for Week 12.

“I’m not going to make any comments about his status until he gets back here,” Vrabel said. “He’s en route back here. He stayed with a few of our people and they’re en route back here. So, once he gets back here, our people are able to visit with him again, talk with him again, I think we’ll have more to offer.

“But I wouldn’t imagine him being available when we come out of the bye.”

PFT reported on Sunday night that Maye is expected to be out for a while, with others reporting on Monday that the quarterback may not be back at all in 2026.

But Vrabel said at this point, he doesn’t expect the team to go and sign another quarterback. Tommy DeVito and and Behren Morton are the other QBs on the 53-man roster. The team does not have a quarterback on the practice squad.

item.title: Vikings won't be leaving Minnesota for altitude acclimation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With quarterback Kirk Cousins back and the Minnesota defense playing at a championship level, the sky is the limit for the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
With quarterback Kirk Cousins back and the Minnesota defense playing at a championship level, the sky is the limit for the Vikings.

On Sunday, the extent to which they'll be literally in the sky could limit the ability to get an eighth win.

The Week 11 prime-time showdown between the 7-2 Vikings and 8-1 49ers will happen in Mexico City, where the altitude is 7,280 feet above sea level. The Vikings won't be relocating this week to acclimate to the thinner air.

The 49ers, in contrast, have gone from Dallas to Colorado, where they'll train in the far lower distance of 5,280 feet above sea level.

The Vikings will have a plan to get their players ready to perform on an elevated field. Details will emerge this week.

Whatever the plan is, it won't entail the same kind of direct acclimation in which the 49ers are engaging.

It sets up another apples-to-apples comparison regarding the plans for international games. In Week 1, the 49ers went to Australia early. The Rams went late. And the 49ers dominated L.A., winning 27-7.

This time around, the stakes are extremely high. The winner takes over the de facto driver's seat for the top seed in the NFC.

A loss means more to the Vikings than the 49ers, as it relates to their respective divisions. San Francisco has a solid cushion over the Seahawks and Rams in the NFC West. The Vikings are caught in a three-way tie for first place in the NFC North.

item.title: Buccaneers add QB Cooper Rush to practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Cooper Rush is headed to a different team in the NFC South.
item.content:encoded:
Cooper Rush is headed to a different team in the NFC South.

With starter Baker Mayfield banged up, Rush is signing with the Buccaneers practice squad, according to agency Equity Sports.

Rush was with the Falcons earlier this season, starting a pair of games with poor results. Rush completed 22-of-39 passes for 229 yards with one touchdown, four interceptions, and a lost fumble.

Atlanta released him last month.

If Mayfield is not able to start this week against the Lions, rookie backup Jalon Daniels would presumably take Mayfield’s place as QB1. Daniels went 1-2 in his three starts while Mayfield was dealing with a thumb injury, completing 61.2 percent of his passes for 501 yards with three touchdowns and five interceptions.

item.title: Sean McVay: Aaron Donald never ceases to amaze me, he's one-of-one
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: For the first time in 1,050 days, Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald recorded a sack when he brought down rookie Carson Beck during the second quarter of Sunday's victory over the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time in 1,050 days, Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald recorded a sack when he brought down rookie Carson Beck during the second quarter of Sunday's victory over the Cardinals.

It was the first of two takedowns he was involved in on the day, as he was also credited for a half-sack later in the afternoon.

After the contest, head coach Sean McVay told reporters Donald “never ceases to amaze me.”

“I’m never surprised,” McVay said in his press conference. “I think the term ‘one-of-one’ is thrown around way too loosely in this day and age, but it’s not with him. He’s one-of-one. He can do things, he’s done things and his impact — whether he has to say it or just show it, he’s a total ‘G.’ I love everything he’s about, and he is one-of-one.

“He’s had a tremendous impact on this team and it certainly is not exclusive to just getting a sack today. He’s made a tremendous impact. He’s a guy that everybody looks at and they say, ‘Watching the way that he moves — if you just mimic and emulate that, we’ll be in good shape.’”

Donald has tallied 15 total tackles with four tackles for loss, four QB hits, and now 1.5 sacks since returning from his retirement at the start of the season.

item.title: Report: Cowboys RG Tyler Booker has a high-ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys may be without right guard Tyler Booker in the coming weeks.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys may be without right guard Tyler Booker in the coming weeks.

Booker left Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers after playing 33 offensive snaps and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that he is dealing with a high-ankle sprain.

High-ankle sprains often lead to multi-week absences and Booker missed three games with a similar injury last season. The Cowboys face the Titans, Eagles and Seahawks before a bye in Week 14.

T.J. Bass took over for the final 50 snaps of Sunday's loss and will likely be at right guard until Booker is cleared to return to action.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey on career-high receiving yards: You just catch it and run as fast as you can
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Christian McCaffrey had a day.
item.content:encoded:
Christian McCaffrey had a day.

The 49ers running back had never had more than 121 receiving yards in a single game. He had 161 receiving yards on four catches Sunday against the Cowboys, scoring on catch-and-runs of 74 and 66 in the 49ers' 46-40 win.

"You never know," McCaffrey said. "You go into each game. You don't really predict anything. Again, you just have to have the right mindset on a play that's going to break. You trust your instincts and play fast."

His first receiving touchdown came when Brock Purdy rolled to his right to buy time and found McCaffrey running free on the scramble drill.

"It really is backyard football at that point," McCaffrey said. "We all played it as kids at recess, and you draw up plays on your hand, and it never happens. You ever tell a 5-year-old to run a post route, and he just runs a corner and something else, but he's open? That's kind of what that was. Again, I think those little decisions that you make in games, from Brock to scramble, not to just surrender the play but to keep it alive. That's a big deal. There's no planning that goes into that. It's just him doing a great job playing ball."

What turned out to be the game-winning touchdown came with 3:23 remaining when Purdy found McCaffrey, who was matched up against Von Miller, over the middle.

"They brought pressure," McCaffrey said. "They dropped a D-end on me, so that's a perfect look for that play. Again, it was a great job by Brock getting the ball where it needed to be. It made it easy for me.

"You just catch it and run as fast as you can to try to score. Don't overthink it. You hope that nobody catches you, and you hope that you're really fast so your teammates don't catch up to you to celebrate, because it makes you look slow. We'll have to check the tape."

McCaffrey had a 16-yard touchdown run and 62 yards rushing. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown.

item.title: Dak Prescott: 49ers fans "were more present than ours"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, America's Team wasn't even Dallas's Team. 49ers fans showed up in big numbers for the game against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, America's Team wasn't even Dallas's Team. 49ers fans showed up in big numbers for the game against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium.

After the game, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott was asked whether the home team had to use the silent count.

"No, we didn't go on the silent count," Prescott said. "[We] anticipated it. I think y'all even potentially asked me on Thursday about it, having this many 49er fans there. Tricked myself and told myself early on that the red was for my high school.

"And at the end of the day, all I asked for is a great environment to play this game. And unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours, but it created a great atmosphere. So, we take the good out of it one way or another."

For owner Jerry Jones, the colors worn by the fans don't matter; their money is the same shade of green.

Still, it's always a bad look when too many fans of the opposing team show up for a road game. On Sunday, 49ers fans found their way to buy tickets and infiltrate the venue.

And their fans got to see the Niners move to 8-1 on the season.

item.title: Mike Macdonald praises Tory Horton's "tremendous play" on late kickoff return
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: After the Raiders cut the Seahawks' lead to 21-13 by kicking a field goal with 2:04 left in Sunday's game, they wanted to force a touchback that would allow them to use the two-minute warning as a third timeout in hopes of getting the ball back.
item.content:encoded:
After the Raiders cut the Seahawks' lead to 21-13 by kicking a field goal with 2:04 left in Sunday's game, they wanted to force a touchback that would allow them to use the two-minute warning as a third timeout in hopes of getting the ball back.

Seahawks wide receiver Tory Horton made sure that didn't happen. Horton perfectly timed a leap that allowed him to bat a kickoff that was sailing long into the end zone. Horton stepped out of bounds upon coming down, so he motioned for Rashid Shaheed to return it into the field of play and Shaheed was tackled with 1:59 left to accomplish the Seahawks' goal of burning the Raiders' extra chance to stop the clock.

Horton was flagged for an illegal bat of the ball, but the Raiders declined the penalty as it would have forced a re-kick that took more time off the clock and head coach Mike Macdonald praised Horton's quick thinking in his postgame press conference.

"It was a tremendous play," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "Tory's actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take [Jadarian Price] off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven't necessarily practiced a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out. . . . We told them that was the situation going. Now, there's a difference between catching it 8 yards deep in the end zone and making a play like that, which is just some really, really great stuff."

The Seahawks were likely to win the game regardless of how the kickoff played out, but Horton made closing things out easier and his effort will be on the minds of many people around the league if they find themselves in a similar situation.

item.title: Aaron Glenn had DC Brian Duker calling Jets defensive plays on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets's eighth loss of the 2026 season had things in common with the previous seven, but Sunday's outing against the Bills was different in one significant way.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets's eighth loss of the 2026 season had things in common with the previous seven, but Sunday's outing against the Bills was different in one significant way.

Head coach Aaron Glenn confirmed at a Monday press conference that he had defensive coordinator Brian Duker calling the defensive plays for the first time this season.

"I gave Duker the lead when it comes to that. I’m still a huge part of what we call," Glenn said.

Glenn said last week that he was "looking at everything" when it came to finding ways for the Jets to improve on their 2-7 start and reiterated on Monday that he is willing to do "anything that I can do as a head coach to help us win games." The Jets gave up 389 yards in the 31-12 loss to the Bills, including 201 rushing yards that included a 74-yard James Cook touchdown run late in the fourth quarter.

Duker's predecessor Steve Wilks was Glenn's initial defensive playcaller in 2025, but he was fired in mid-December and Glenn announced he would take over that responsibility in the offseason. Glenn had called the plays as the Lions' defensive coordinator and called that his "superpower" in February, but opposing offenses have proven to be his kryptonite far too often during the 2026 season.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes on his injured elbow: Obviously, it felt good enough
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered a right elbow injury during the Week 9 victory over the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered a right elbow injury during the Week 9 victory over the Jets.

While it looked bad initially, it certainly didn’t seem to affect him in yesterday’s 35-13 victory over the Falcons.

Despite missing Kenneth Walker and dealing with other injuries on offense, Mahomes threw five touchdowns in a single game for the first time since 2022. He ended the victory 22-of-35 for 348 yards with no interceptions.

So how was his elbow feeling during the game?

“Obviously, it felt good enough,” Mahomes said in his postgame press conference. “I was a little nervous going into the game, just because it was a little sore. But we did a great job, [Chiefs assistant athletic trainer] Julie [Frymer], and the whole training staff did a great job all week of just trying to make sure that I was in a great spot to go out there and compete, and I was able to do that today.

“I'm sure we'll have some ice on it going back home. But we'll continue that same process this next week, and try to get it as healthy as possible, as quickly as possible.”

What was he nervous about?

“I didn't feel like during the week of practice, I was driving the ball the way I wanted to,” Mahomes said. “Just because of some of those deeper in-cut routes and the different balls down the field, you don't know until you get out there, that adrenaline starts kicking a little bit.

“And obviously, it was good enough.”

Mahomes now has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,385 yards with 19 touchdowns and four interceptions this season. His 106.7 passer rating is his highest since 2022, when he finished at 105.2 and won his second MVP award.

item.title: Dolphins waive Zane Gonzalez after three missed kicks on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Dolphins are looking for a new kicker.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins are looking for a new kicker.

They announced that they have waived Zane Gonzalez on Monday. The move comes a day after Gonzalez had a hand in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts.

Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point as Miami fell to 1-8 on the season. That loss came despite the Dolphins picking up more yards than the Colts while winning the turnover battle and committing three penalties while the Colts were flagged 13 times.

It was Gonzalez's fourth game with the Dolphins this season. He was a practice squad elevation for the first three appearances and the team will have someone else handling those duties in Buffalo in Week 11.

item.title: Panthers on pace to set new NFL records for most penalties and penalty yards this season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Panthers beat the Saints on Sunday despite being assessed a whopping 17 penalties for 152 yards.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers beat the Saints on Sunday despite being assessed a whopping 17 penalties for 152 yards. If they keep it up, they're going to end this season with more penalties and more penalty yards than any team has ever had.

Through nine games, the Panthers lead the NFL with 87 penalties for 787 yards. That puts them on pace for 164 penalties for 1,487 yards in 17 games, both of which would be new NFL records. The current NFL records were set by the 2011 Oakland Raiders, who were assessed 163 penalties for 1,358 yards.

Panthers coach Dave Canales said after Sunday's game that he can accept some penalties that are naturally going to happen over the course of a game, but he doesn't accept mental mistakes like jumping offside.

"Some of the penalties that are judgment calls, they're gonna call them how they see them," Canales said. "The things that I'm gonna focus on are the ones we have to take control of, which are offside penalties, pre-snap, delay of games, those type of procedural penalties. We've got to eliminate those. The competitive calls are going to happen. There's ways to talk about the technique, but it's really the things that we can control that we have to focus on."

Asked if he had a problem with the officials on Sunday, who assessed the Saints just three penalties while the Panthers got 17, Canales answered, "I'm not gonna get into that."

Canales did address the penalties with his team, however.

"We talked about the penalties. We set a new franchise record with 17, and we have to fix that. That's not gonna be sustainable in this league, when the margins are so tight. The guys understand that," Canales said.

What Canales will do is address what his own team can do better, perhaps improving enough over the second half of the season to avoid breaking a record that no coach wants to break.

item.title: ACC announces punishments after Louisville-North Carolina brawl
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The ACC has spoken.
item.content:encoded:
The ACC has spoken.

After Saturday night's brawl at the end of the game between Louisville and North Carolina, the conference has issued a statement listing the "suspensions, institutional fines, and public reprimands" arising from the incident.

"The unsportsmanlike behavior displayed was unacceptable," the conference said, "and each institution will incur a fine."

The amounts of the fines were not disclosed.

The ACC also has suspended Louisville linebacker Stanquan Clark and North Carolina defensive back Greg Smith III for the first half of their programs' next games.

Without knowing the fines, it's impossible to know how significant the punishments were. The fact that only two players will miss only one half of a game seems to be on the light side of the range of consequences that could have been issued to the players.

The incident was sparked by North Carolina's Schiano-style attack against Louisville's effort to end the game in victory formation. It was a confusing degree of aggression/desperation, given that the Tar Heels had a timeout that they did not use.

It was quite possibly frustration from UNC after falling short in their effort to get a sixth win and, in turn, to become bowl-eligible.

item.title: Jaguars improve to 7-2 with 40-23 win over Titans
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Jaguars didn't play their best game of the season today in Tennessee, but they didn't need to to beat the Titans.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars didn't play their best game of the season today in Tennessee, but they didn't need to to beat the Titans.

In a game the Jaguars sleepwalked through for some long stretches, Trevor Lawrence still ended up with 352 passing yards and three touchdowns, and the Jaguars still covered the 10.5-point spread in a 40-23 win.

Lawrence hit Parker Washington in the end zone for a touchdown on the first possession of the game, and it looked like it would be a cakewalk for the Jaguars.

But Cam Ward made some plays both running and passing, and Tony Pollard turned a short pass into a 32-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter, and the Titans kept it to within one score for much of the game. Ultimately, however, the Titans just couldn't hold this Jaguars team in check for 60 minutes.

Few opponents have managed to hold the Jaguars in check for 60 minutes. Today's win improves their record to 7-2, and they're poised to make a run for the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs.

The Titans fall to 1-8, and they're poised to make a run for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.

item.title: Josh Downs "excited to keep building" connection with Patrick Mahomes
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs didn't waste any time making an impact for his new team.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs wide receiver Josh Downs didn't waste any time making an impact for his new team.

Downs joined the Chiefs in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday, which meant that he had limited practice time with quarterback Patrick Mahomes ahead of Sunday's game in Atlanta. Their lack of familiarity with one another didn't get in the way of Downs hauling in an 18-yard touchdown pass from the quarterback in the second quarter and he finished his Kansas City debut with four catches for 53 yards.

"Pat gave me a chance, and I went up and made a play," Downs said, via Nate Taylor of ESPN.com. "I'm excited to keep building off of that. First game and first touchdown, you can't write it better than that. Playing with a guy like him is incredible. Doing anything you can to get open for him and making plays is what I want to do."

Downs only played 10 offensive snaps in the 35-13 Chiefs win, which makes his production stand out all the more. It also leads to thoughts of what his connection with Mahomes will look like once they've had more time working with one another and those thoughts will be pleasant ones for Chiefs fans to ponder heading into Week 11.

item.title: Geno Smith getting tests on ankle, will start in Week 11 if healthy
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets quarterback Geno Smith was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Bills with an ankle injury and his status for Week 11 is still to be determined.
item.content:encoded:
Jets quarterback Geno Smith was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Bills with an ankle injury and his status for Week 11 is still to be determined.

Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters at a Monday press conference that Smith is having tests on his ankle on Monday. Smith missed one series earlier in the game to have a concussion evaluation and left the game for good after hurting his ankle in the third quarter.

Glenn confirmed that Smith will remain the team's starter against the Chargers if he is cleared medically. Rookie Cade Klubnik made his regular season debut on Sunday and will make his first NFL start if Smith is unable to play.

Rookie wideout Omar Cooper also left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and he'll go for tests on Monday as well.

item.title: Report: Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with torn ACL, likely additional damage
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Hutchinson suffered the season-ending injury while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye, who was also injured.
item.content:encoded:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season with a serious knee injury he suffered while celebrating a sack on Sunday.

Hutchinson has a torn ACL in his right knee and probably additional damage, according to Ian Rapoport.

The torn ACL was seen on the MRI he had in Germany after leaving Sunday's game, and the team plans to give him additional tests now that he's back in Detroit. There are concerns that he also injured his meniscus.

Hutchinson is one of the best defensive players in the NFL and his loss is devastating to the Lions, who are 7-2 and have legitimate Super Bowl hopes. They also had legitimate Super Bowl hopes two years ago, when Hutchinson suffered a season-ending broken leg, and their defense wasn't the same without him.

The injury came moments after Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye. Hutchinson got up, jumped in the air celebrating, and landed awkwardly, with his right knee seeming to buckle. He immediately went to the ground and grabbed his leg.

Maye was also injured on the play, missed the rest of the game and is likely out for a significant period of time.

item.title: Joe Burrow becomes the MVP favorite
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is having a potentially historic season.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is having a potentially historic season. And, to no surprise, his performance has vaulted him past Bills quarterback Josh Allen as the favorite for the NFL MVP award.

After registering a fifth straight game with four or more total touchdowns — matching Peyton Manning (2004) as the only two players to ever do that — Burrow has surged to a +105 favorite to win the MVP trophy.

Along the way, the Bengals blasted the Steelers, 38-18. Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns, as Cincinnati outgained Pittsburgh, 484 to 222.

Allen is second in the current odds, at +310. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy lurks at +400, with Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence at +500.

There's a gap after those four, with Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes at 16-1. (Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who arguably best fits the official Associated Press definition of the term, remains an 80-1 long shot.)

The voting, which happens in the days after Week 18, will undoubtedly be influenced by the final configuration of the AFC and NFC playoff trees. Getting the top seed will give the quarterbacks of those teams a boost.

In the AFC, rhat could be the Bengals. Or the Bills. Or the Jaguars. Or the Chiefs. In the NFC, it could be the 49ers.

For now, Burrow has laid the foundation for a stretch run that earns his first career MVP award.

item.title: Panthers pull out 20-17 win in New Orleans, take lead in NFC South
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: NFC South football has earned a negative reputation over the last few years and Sunday's game between the Panthers and Saints didn't do much to change that, but it did push one of the teams into first place in the race to represent the division in the playoffs.
item.content:encoded:
NFC South football has earned a negative reputation over the last few years and Sunday's game between the Panthers and Saints didn't do much to change that, but it did push one of the teams into first place in the race to represent the division in the playoffs.

After the Saints rallied to tie the game on a Charlie Smyth field goal with 41 seconds left to play, the Panthers took over on their own 34-yard-line. Bryce Young threw an incompletion and then uncorked a deep shot to wide receiver Jalen Coker. Saints corner Kool-Aid McKinstry was flagged for pass interference and that set up a 54-yard field goal as time expired.

Ryan Fitzgerald had missed from 48 yards in the first half, but he nailed this kick and the Panthers are in first place after a 20-17 win.

There's some irony in the fact that a penalty helped put the Panthers in position to win the game. Carolina committed 17 penalties during the contest, including a facemask call on linebacker Tyrel Dodson that helped set up Smyth's game-tying kick.

The Saints did their best to match that sloppiness with a pair of turnovers in the first half and they focused on the running game well beyond the point when it became clear that they weren't going to generate the kind of production needed on that front. Travis Etienne, Audric Estime, and Alvin Kamara combined to pick up 24 yards on 17 carries on Sunday.

Their offense picked up a bit once they leaned on throwing the ball and rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson wound up with 11 catches in his second game of the year, but the overall approach was still lacking against a Panthers team that has not been very stout defensively this season.

New Orleans will be in Chicago next Sunday and they'll need a win there to try to keep themselves in stalking distance of the Panthers heading into the stretch run.

Carolina improved to 4-5 with the win and they will host the Ravens in Week 11. They'd be wise to continue leaning on Chuba Hubbard in that contest. Hubbard had 27 carries for 92 yards and two touchdowns along with five catches for 80 yards. That accounted for 172 of the Panthers' 283 total yards, so Carolina's best chance of winning games appears to be relying on their workhorse running back.

item.title: Aaron Glenn could become sixth coach to start 0-9 in division
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Jets coach Aaron Glenn has a 5-21 record during his one-and-a-half-year tenure with the team.
item.content:encoded:
Jets coach Aaron Glenn has a 5-21 record during his one-and-a-half-year tenure with the team. That's bad.

Here's something worse: Glenn is 0-8 in AFC East games.

That's the longest active losing streak in the division by any team. And it's one game short of putting Glenn in a small club that no one wants to belong to.

A loss on Sunday to the Bills would make Glenn the sixth head coach since the 1970 merger to start his career 0-9 in division games. The others were Jim Schwartz (0-10), Matt Eberflus (0-9), Pat Shurmur (0-9), John McKay (0-9), and Jim Ringo (0-9).

With each additional loss, the question becomes whether it will be Glenn's final loss. The clock seems to be ticking toward an in-season termination. Or, if owner Woody Johnson doesn't decide to make a move before Week 18, an abrupt parting of ways after the season ends.

item.title: Deshaun Watson found it "definitely special" to beat the Texans
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter on Sunday, which isn't surprising given the way the 2026 season has unfolded in Cleveland.
item.content:encoded:
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson led a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter on Sunday, which isn't surprising given the way the 2026 season has unfolded in Cleveland.

All six of the team's wins have come thanks to Watson's efforts in the final minutes and the Browns are the first team in league history to win its first six games of a season by four points or fewer. Sunday's 27-24 win did have a different wrinkle for the quarterback, however. It came against the Texans, who drafted Watson in 2017 and then traded him to the Browns in 2022 after Watson sat out the 2021 season amid sexual misconduct allegations and a trade request.

Watson said that the opponent meant that beating his former team was "definitely special" for him.

“I think people know the history behind it," Watson said, via a transcript from the team. "Didn’t leave on a good note, but it’s all love for the city of Houston, the fans there, the players there, some of the staff there, most definitely, that I got to see today. And even the older ownership. So, it was good to see a lot of people, familiar faces, but it’s still love. But it’s definitely a good win.”

Watson's time with the Texans is in the past and the present is exciting for the Browns. They head into their bye week with a 6-4 record that has them firmly in playoff contention and Sunday's win gave them their first 4-0 home start to a season since 1963. Faster starts would likely help their chances of both staying unbeaten at home and making it to the postseason, but knowing that they're never out of a game isn't a bad lesson to take from the first 10 weeks of the season.

item.title: Joe Burrow: Sunday night was great, but you're not winning anything after nine games
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow entered some rare company in Sunday night's romp over the Steelers.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow entered some rare company in Sunday night's romp over the Steelers.

Burrow's four touchdown passes gave him 20 over the last five games and that's something that only Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have accomplished over the history of the league. Both of those players have won MVP awards and Burrow is now the frontrunner for that award for the current season.

The crowd in Cincinnati picked up on that and chanted "MVP" for Burrow during the 38-18 win and Burrow acknowledged the run he's been on during a postgame press conference. Burrow said "a great one" when asked what kind of quarterback he was on Sunday, but noted it's "a long season" when asked about the MVP conversation and that the team's goals are equally unrealized at this point in the year.

"No one is winning the division with seven wins," Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. "Nobody's making the playoffs with seven wins, and we're certainly not satisfied."

Burrow may not want to look ahead at this point, but others will do it for him and the Bengals' schedule is set up for them to continue stacking wins as long as they remain in the groove they've been in on their current five-game streak. If they do that, there will likely be a lot of people who believe Burrow can join Brady and Manning as both MVPs and Super Bowl champs.
